papers.title_en: LSRP*-LA: Scalable and Anytime Multi-Agent Path Finding for Large Agents with Asynchronous Actions
papers.authors: Dachuan Liu, Shizhe Zhao, Zhongqiang Ren
papers.evidence: 面向大型智能体异步动作的可扩展任意时间MAPF
papers.tldr: 多智能体路径规划常假设单格智能体与同步动作，难以用于大体积智能体场景。本文提出LSRP*-LA，面向大智能体异步动作的LA-MAPF-AA，可扩展、完备并支持任意时间持续优化解。在多种地图上最多800个智能体的实验中，其可处理智能体数约为基线两倍，解成本约为近期同步大智能体规划器的一半。该工作扩展了LSRP*，提升了大智能体异步MAPF的实用性与解质量。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents from their start locations to their goal locations while minimizing path costs. Most MAPF algorithms assume that each agent occupies a single vertex and that the actions of all agents are synchronized. These assumptions may limit the use of MAPF planners in practice. Existing planners that get rid of both assumptions either handle only a few agents or cannot improve their solutions. Recently, a planner called LSRP* was proposed, which is scalable and anytime with asynchronous actions, but still limited by that each agent occupies a single vertex. This paper develops a new planner called LSRP*-LA for MAPF for large agents with asynchronous actions (LA-MAPF-AA), where an agent can occupy several cells. LSRP*-LA is scalable and complete, and it keeps improving solution quality after the initial solution is obtained until the runtime budget depletes. We analyze the properties of LSRP*-LA and test it against several baselines with up to 800 agents on various maps. LSRP*-LA can handle twice as many agents as baseline methods and its solution cost is about half that of recent synchronous planners for large agents.

papers.title_en: Energy-Aware Distributed Task Allocation via Local Submodular Maximization
papers.authors: Jing Liu, Fangfei Li, Xin Jin, Yang Tang, Ruggero Carli, Luca Ballotta
papers.evidence: 面向智能体团队的分布式任务分配与邻居冲突消解
papers.tldr: 针对动态智能体、任务与通信图下的分布式任务分配，论文将每轮分配建模为带分区拟阵约束的单调子模最大化，并提出DAGBA：局部可行集构建、条件边际竞价与邻居冲突消解。理论上证明逐轮可行、有限轮收敛与剩余能量安全，并在顺序贪心情形恢复1/2近似，一般情形给出局部信息因子及可计算保守界。仿真显示任务完成进度与效用接近集中式/全通信基准，同时提升通信效率并保持严格能量可行。
papers.abstract_en: This paper studies distributed task allocation under time-varying agent sets, task sets, and communication graphs. At each decision epoch, the stage allocation problem is formulated as monotone submodular maximization over a time-varying, energy-filtered admissible ground set subject to a partition-matroid constraint. We develop a Distributed Adaptive Greedy Bidding Algorithm (DAGBA) that combines local admissible-set construction, conditional marginal bidding, and neighbor-based conflict resolution under limited communication. We prove that DAGBA guarantees per-epoch feasibility, finite-round convergence, and residual-energy safety. Theoretically, we identify a sequential-greedy regime where DAGBA recovers the classical $1/2$-approximation guarantee. For general executions with partial information, we derive a local-information-factor approximation bound and conservative bounds computable from the execution trace that quantify the degradation caused by local estimates and parallel fixing. Simulations on cooperative observation missions demonstrate that DAGBA achieves task-completion progress and utility close to centralized and complete-communication references, while improving communication efficiency and maintaining strict energy feasibility.

papers.title_en: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-UAV Data Harvesting Under Variable Team Sizes and Agent Loss
papers.authors: Thiago de Souza Lamenza, Bruno José Olivieri de Souza, Markus Endler
papers.evidence: 面向无人机编队协同的多智能体强化学习
papers.tldr: 针对通信设施受限时无线传感器数据难以回传的问题，无人机编队可依托移动性进行本地采集，但不同团队规模与智能体永久损失会使固定规模多智能体策略失效。本文提出F-MADDPG，在MADDPG框架下支持可变数量传感器与无人机，并适配任务中智能体灾难性失效。实验表明其可跨种群规模学习，平均任务完成快于MLP版MADDPG基线，逆基数团队规模采样优于均匀采样，且在永久损失后仍有效。该工作提升了多无人机数据采集策略的灵活性与鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Collecting data from wireless sensors can be challenging when limited communication infrastructure prevents them from offloading their measurements. In such settings, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can exploit their mobility to harvest data locally, while coordinated UAV teams can provide efficient and redundant coverage of remote areas. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables such teams to learn decentralized coordination policies. However, training separate policies for different team and sensor populations is costly, and fixed-population policies may be vulnerable to agent failures. This work proposes F-MADDPG, a flexible variant of Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) that supports data harvesting with varying numbers of wireless sensors and UAVs. The framework also accommodates unexpected catastrophic failures that permanently remove agents during a mission. We compare F-MADDPG with a MADDPG baseline that uses multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and evaluate training strategies based on team-size sampling and exposure to agent terminations. The results show that F-MADDPG learns across the evaluated population sizes, completes missions faster than the baseline on average, benefits from inverse-cardinality team-size sampling compared with uniform sampling, remains effective after permanent agent losses, and gains no consistent benefit from exposure to failures during training.

papers.title_en: CoTAMP: Cooperative Task and Motion Planning for Quadruped Robots with Large Language Models
papers.evidence: 多四足机器人协同任务与运动规划
papers.tldr: 单四足机器人难以通过需协作的复杂地形，现有方法多局限于单机运动或预定义技能。CoTAMP将协作任务与运动规划拆成任务规划和运动生成两部分，结合LLM模块与代码模块发明新动作、生成关键帧并经运动学综合与轨迹优化得到动力学可行轨迹。在三个仿真课程、两种RAIBO2模型上，30次试验均生成运动学有效参考并全部通过轨迹优化收敛。相比基线，其在成功率、动态可行性、执行时间与生成成本上更具优势。
papers.abstract_en: Some environments cannot be traversed by a single quadruped robot, for example a ledge that one robot can climb only from its partner's back or a gap that must be bridged with boxes. Solving them requires cooperative task and motion planning (TAMP). Previous works are limited to the motions of a single robot or only select actions from a predefined set of skills. We propose a framework with two parts: task planning that invents motions not defined in advance, and motion generation that realizes the invented motions. Both parts consist of large language model (LLM)-based modules and code-based modules. Task planning divides the trajectory of the whole task into steps and fixes the robot poses at the step boundaries. Motion generation produces keyframes that describe the motion of each step and turns them into a continuous trajectory through kinematic synthesis. The code-based modules check every plan and motion and return failures to the LLM-based modules for correction. The whole trajectory is then refined by trajectory optimization to satisfy the dynamics. On three simulated courses with two RAIBO2 robot models, our framework produced kinematically valid references in all 30 trials, all of which converged in trajectory optimization. Compared with several baselines, our framework showed advantages in success rate, dynamic feasibility, execution time, and generation time and cost. Project page: https://woojin8098.github.io/CoTAMP/

papers.title_en: Compute-Aware Submodular Online Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
papers.authors: Jing Liu, Luca Ballotta, Fangfei Li, Yang Tang, Ruggero Carli
papers.evidence: 多智能体协作任务分配策略学习
papers.tldr: 开放多智能体系统协作任务分配中，子模效用导致边际收益递减，逐候选动作评估的在线策略更新计算开销过高。为此，方法对规定数量的智能体-动作对采样，并用逆概率加权边际增益，构造期望阶段效用的无偏梯度，驱动 KL 镜像上升更新。理论上给出 1/2 近似遗憾界，将其分解为策略间 KL 跟踪误差与查询相关反馈项。协作信息覆盖实验表明，该方法在显著减少在线计算的同时保持高性能。
papers.abstract_en: This paper studies policy learning for cooperative task allocation in open multi-agent systems, where submodular utilities model diminishing marginal returns due to overlapping agent contributions. While standard methods evaluate every candidate action to update the policy, this may incur an excessive computational cost online. Hence, we impose a budget on these evaluations and analytically study the effect of query budget on online learning. Our algorithm samples a prescribed number of agent-action pairs and applies inverse-probability weighting to their marginal gains, yielding an unbiased gradient estimate of the expected stage utility for a Kullback-Leibler (KL) mirror-ascent update. We derive a $1/2$-approximate regret bound that elegantly splits into a tracking error between optimal and learned policies, quantified by their KL divergence, and a query-dependent feedback term. Experiments on cooperative information coverage show that our approach retains high performance with significantly less computation online.
